contracts.declarative.ResourceMetadata.description:
Common metadata for all declarative resources.

# Fields

- `name`: Resource local identifier (resolver input for identity mapping)
- `description`: Human-readable description
- `tags`: Key-value pairs for filtering and organization
- `annotations`: Key-value pairs for extended metadata (not used for filtering)
- `providerRef`: The Provider the resource is filed under

name.description:
Resource name.

This is a service-scoped local identifier used by declarative identity mapping.
The final TRN resource path is resolver-derived and may compose additional
namespace context. Workspace filename matching, if required, is a loader/workspace
policy and not a contracts-level invariant.

tags.description:
Tags for filtering and organization.

Tags are key-value pairs that can be used for:
- Filtering resources in queries
- Organizing resources by environment, team, etc.

annotations.description:
Annotations for extended metadata.

Unlike tags, annotations are not used for filtering.
They're meant for storing additional metadata like:
- Creation tool information
- External system references
- Custom metadata

providerRef.description:
The Provider this resource is filed under, as a ProviderHub Provider
TRN of the resource's own tenant.

It only files the resource for filtering and display; it never
changes how the resource runs. A Provider resource carries none.

contracts.declarative.ResourceTrn.description:
A validated literal TRN reference — the final scalar value of every
declarative reference field.

contracts.declarative.FunctionSpec.description:
Function specification.

Single source of truth for function authoring intent.
Same structure used in workspace YAML, API JSON, and server.

`source` is declarative authoring input only. Execution truth is the
immutable version binding created during publish; executors and runtimes
must not execute directly from `FunctionSpec.source`.

# Workspace Example (YAML)

```yaml
service: aionixfn
resourceType: function
metadata:
  name: my-function
spec:
  serviceAccountRef: trn:iam:tenant:test0001:service-account/function-my-function-runner
  runtime: deno2
  handler: main.ts:handler
  env:
    LOG_LEVEL: info
```

# API Example (JSON)

```json
{
  "serviceAccountRef": "trn:iam:tenant:test0001:service-account/function-my-function-runner",
  "runtime": "deno2",
  "handler": "main.ts:handler",
  "env": { "LOG_LEVEL": "info" }
}
```

serviceAccountRef.description:
Runtime identity used by this function.

Optional: absent means this workload has NO runtime identity — no
runtime credentials are minted and every outbound platform call fails
closed. Declare one ServiceAccount reference exactly when the
workload calls the platform; permissions attach to that
ServiceAccount through Auth policies, not here.

runtime.description: The runtime that runs the code: `bun1`, `deno2` or `python3.14`.

handler.description:
The entry point, in colon format. For `bun1` and `deno2` it is a module
file and one of its exports: `main.ts:handler`, `main.ts:default`.
For `python3.14` it is a module and a function: `main:handler`.

layerRefs.description:
The Layers the Function composes, named by TRN and kept as written: a
stable TRN follows the Layer's current version at every invocation, a
`v<n>` TRN pins one version. Entries normalize to canonical TRN order;
their authored order never grants content shadowing priority.

env.description:
Literal string configuration exposed to the handler through context.env.
Values are versioned and never interpreted as expressions or injected
into the host process environment.

inputSchema.description:
Caller-facing input contract (JSON Schema Draft 2020-12). Every submit
and synchronous execute validates its input against the selected
version's Schema when the invocation is admitted; a violation rejects
it with `InputSchemaViolation` and nothing is queued or run.

execution.description: Workload execution policy selected for function invocation attempts.

source.description:
Declarative authoring source intent.

Defines where the published inputs come from. This is not executable runtime
truth. Runnable execution must use the immutable version binding created
during publish.

# Example

```yaml
source:
  type: directory
  location: src
```

contracts.aionixfn.RuntimeId.description: Identifier of an installed runtime contract profile, such as deno2.

contracts.aionixfn.LayerReference.description:
A stable or pinned AionixFn Layer TRN written in a Function declaration.
It is kept as written; every invocation resolves it when it is admitted.

contracts.core.ProfiledWorkloadExecution.description:
A [`WorkloadExecutionPolicy`] of a workload that chooses where it runs: a
named execution profile, without one the deployment's default, and the
worker resource class its attempts are routed to.

resourceClass.description:
The worker resource class the workload's attempts are routed to. The
class's resource envelope (CPU, memory, process count, scratch space,
open files) is enforced only by an isolated execution boundary; a
local boundary uses the class for routing alone and enforces none of
those limits.

oneOf.description: Local directory prepared by CLI or Studio before upload.
Local ZIP file uploaded by CLI or Studio.
Local single source file packaged by CLI or Studio.

contracts.declarative.PackagePath.description: Path relative to the package root using '/' separators; surrounding whitespace, '.', '..', empty segments, absolute paths and drive prefixes are rejected.
